Declare rules a table must satisfy, and check them

Source: R/rul.R
rul.Rd

rul() declares one rule: a name, a function that says whether the data pass, the column it reads (or the whole table), how serious a failure is and the message to give. valrules() runs a list of rules on a data frame and returns the ones that failed, with the rows that broke them. The ready-made rules (ruleinset() and the others) cover the usual checks, so that they are written once and not by hand.

Usage

rul(name, expr, col = NULL, sev = c("warning", "fatal"), msg = NULL)

valrules(data, rules)

Arguments

name

The rule's name: one non-empty string. It names the rule in the result.

expr

A function of one argument that returns TRUE/FALSE for the table or one logical value per row.

col

The column the rule reads, or NULL (the default) for a rule on the whole data frame.

sev

"warning" (the default) or "fatal": how serious a failure is. valrules() records it; the caller decides what follows.

msg

The message of a failure, or NULL for "Rule '' failed".

data

The table the rules are run on: a data frame.

rules

One rule or a list of rules.

Value

rul() an object of class clrule, a list: rule ("fn"), name, col (when given), sev, msg and expr. valrules() an object of class valrules: a list with one element per failed rule, named by the rule, each a list of severity, message and, for a row-wise rule, nfail (the number of failing rows) and rows (the first ten of them). A table that passes every rule gives an empty list.

Details

The function expr receives the column col as a vector, or the whole data frame when col is NULL. It returns either one TRUE or FALSE for the table, or one value per row; in the row-wise form a missing answer counts as a failure, since a rule that cannot decide has not been met. A rule for a column the table does not have is skipped. A rule whose function stops with an error, or returns something that is not logical, is reported as a failure that says so: a broken rule never passes silently. Two rules of one name leave one entry, the later one.

A ready-made rule holds no function: it is a list of its kind (rule) and what it was given, and valrules() also takes it written by hand, as list(rule = "btw", col = "year", lo = 2000, hi = 2026). That form is the one the other languages of the package use, where valrules() and the ready-made rules exist too; a rule made by rul() holds an R function and runs in R only.

Errors: a name or col that is not one non-empty string; expr not a function; sev not "warning" or "fatal"; data not a data frame; rules not a rule or a list of rules.

References

van der Loo, M. P. J. and de Jonge, E. (2021). Data validation infrastructure for R. Journal of Statistical Software, 97(10), 1-31. doi:10.18637/jss.v097.i10

de Jonge, E. and van der Loo, M. (2018). Statistical Data Cleaning with Applications in R. Wiley. doi:10.1002/9781118897126

See also

ruleinset() for the ready-made rules; catchk() and prechk() for other checks before an analysis.

Examples

d <- data.frame(id = c(1, 2, 2, 4), age = c(34, -1, 51, NA),
                charge = c("assault", "theft", "theft", "arson"))
r <- list(
  rul("age_not_negative", function(v) is.na(v) | v >= 0, col = "age",
      msg = "an age is negative"),
  ruleuniq("id", sev = "fatal"),
  rulenull("age"),
  ruleinset("charge", c("assault", "theft", "drugs"))
)
v <- valrules(d, r)
v
#> valrules: 4 rules, 4 failed (1 fatal)
#>   warning  age_not_negative: an age is negative (1 of 4 rows); rows 2
#>   fatal  id_unique: Column 'id' has duplicate values (1 of 4 rows); rows 3
#>   warning  age_not_null: Column 'age' has missing values (1 of 4 rows); rows 4
#>   warning  charge_in_set: Column 'charge' has values outside the allowed set (1 of 4 rows); rows 4
v[["id_unique"]][["rows"]]
#> [1] 3
# a table that passes
length(valrules(d[1, ], r))
#> [1] 0
# a rule written as data
valrules(d, list(rule = "btw", col = "age", lo = 0, hi = 120))
#> valrules: 1 rules, 1 failed (0 fatal)
#>   warning  age_between: Column 'age' has values outside [0, 120] (1 of 4 rows); rows 2
try(rul("", function(v) TRUE))
#> Error : rul: `name` must be one non-empty string.
